positions.pos: The studio boat is a tall ship cut open lengthwise and drawn as a 3D object in one fixed 2D view, Monument Valley style. Every deck keeps the flat boat's rule: one open corridor along the cut where crew are always in view, and five open stairways join the decks. Cabins have no front wall and their side walls reach only halfway forward, so a crew member stays visible for the whole trip, mid-climb included. This replaces lb-keep-the-deck and stands unless you flip it.

Perhaps the tall ship is 3 dimensional but represented in 2d (monument valley style)", with your keep list from ts-ship-look-1. Moving mock: https://claude.ai/artifact/9W13HHYCqpNQcKyDqbDMb3

positions.pos: Four decks, top to keel. Top deck: you at the wheel on the stern castle, the bell on the main mast, the Everdoor in the forecastle for finished strands. Stage deck: the seven stages from Concept at the stern to Release at the bow, each strand's spirit in the cabin of its stage. Workshop deck: the six departments of round 3, where crew live. Hold: the vein of qi, where Tap the vein happens and crew carry qi up. A crate is tinted with the stage it is going to. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Keeps ts-stage-rooms' pipeline order and ty-boat-departments' halls, and puts your bw-crew-are-hands, bw-spirit-is-strand and bw-board-keeps-the-rest steers in places on the ship. Mock: https://claude.ai/artifact/9W13HHYCqpNQcKyDqbDMb3

positions.pos: The pennants are dropped. They were a string of seven flags meant to show the pipeline stages over the flat deck. The stage deck now shows the stages itself, because each crate goes to the cabin of its stage. This answers lb-stage-pennants and stands unless you flip it.
